definition: Similarity learning is an area of supervised machine learning in artificial intelligence.
details: It is closely related to regression and classification, but the goal is to learn a similarity function that measures how similar or related two objects are. It has applications in ranking, in recommendation systems, visual identity tracking, face verification, and speaker verification.

explainer.lead: Similarity learning trains a model to judge how alike two objects are rather than assigning each a fixed label. That makes it useful wherever the task is comparing pairs, such as verifying identities or ranking results.

tiers.eli5: Instead of learning the name of every face, you learn what makes two faces look like the same person.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train on pairs or triplets so that matching items land close in embedding space and non-matching ones pull apart. A pitfall is class imbalance in pairs, which can push the model toward always answering 'similar' or 'different'.
tiers.paperLevel: The goal is to learn a similarity function from labelled pairs; it relates to regression and classification but outputs a relatedness score rather than a class.

explainer.example: A face verification system is trained on same-person and different-person photo pairs so it can score whether two new photos show one person.
